choices.content: a quadrilateral with no special properties

question.prompt: Each angle of a rectangle is trisected. The intersections of the pairs of trisectors adjacent to the same side always form:

solutions.explanation:
Reflection symmetry identifies the usual quadrilateral, but we must also check whether its vertices can coincide. Label the rectangle \(ABCD\) in order, with \(AB\) horizontal. Write \(AB=w>0\), \(BC=h>0\), and let \(O\) be its center. Call the intersections associated with sides \(AB,BC,CD,DA\) respectively \(P,Q,R,S\).

Suppose first that the four points are distinct. Reflection in the vertical midline fixes \(P,R\) and exchanges \(Q,S\). Reflection in the horizontal midline fixes \(Q,S\) and exchanges \(P,R\). Consequently, \(P,R\) lie on one midline and \(Q,S\) on the other, with each pair having midpoint \(O\). These reflections also give
\[
PQ=QR=RS=SP.
\]
Thus the four distinct points form a rhombus, giving choice D in this case.

To find when distinctness fails, notice that the trisectors adjacent to \(AB\) make \(30^\circ\) angles with \(AB\). Their intersection \(P\) lies above its midpoint. In a \(30^\circ\)-\(60^\circ\)-\(90^\circ\) triangle, a short leg \(u\) gives hypotenuse \(2u\) and, by Pythagoras, long leg \(\sqrt3u\). Hence the height of \(P\) above \(AB\) is
\[
\frac{w}{2\sqrt3}.
\]
The reflected points \(P,R\) coincide exactly when both are \(O\), which occurs when
\[
\frac{w}{2\sqrt3}=\frac h2,
\quad\text{or}\quad w=\sqrt3h.
\]
Similarly, \(Q=S=O\) exactly when \(h=\sqrt3w\). Points on different midlines could coincide only at \(O\), so these account for every possible coincidence.

For example, a rectangle with \(w=\sqrt3\) and \(h=1\) has \(P=R=O\), while \(Q,S\) lie on the horizontal midline. The result has three distinct collinear points, not a quadrilateral. Therefore D is valid with the additional condition \(w/h\notin\{\sqrt3,1/\sqrt3\}\); the word “always” makes the statement false as written.
solutions.title: Use reflection symmetry and check for collapse
